name: gpt2_124m
description: GPT-2 124M decoder-only transformer, the LLM the fabric is sized to host
notes: Megatron tensor parallelism: QKV and c_fc column-parallel, out-proj and c_proj row-parallel.
Each layer ends its attention and MLP blocks with one all-reduce of a [1, d_model] activation, so decode pays n_layer * 2 all-reduces per token.
Activations travel as 8-byte IEEE doubles end to end, matching the fabric simulator, so every all-reduce check is exact; a real deployment would use fp16 or fp32 and halve or quarter the traffic.

weight_bits and activation_bits describe the int8 deployment quantization of the matmuls; specgen.py derives the MAC chiplet datapath from them and the accumulator width from the longest dot-product reduction.

seq_len is the modeled decode context: the KV cache holds n_layer * 2 * d_model * seq_len activation-width entries per replica, attention reads it fully per token, and attention-vs-cache MACs (2 * seq_len * d_model per layer) are charged on top of the projection MACs.

Batch-1 decode identity: every block weight is used exactly once per token, so per-token block MACs equal block parameter count, and weight traffic per token equals per_token_macs * weight_bits / 8 bytes. The LM head and embeddings are excluded from both compute and traffic (modeled as host-side).

batch_size 8 with target_tokens_per_s 320 encodes the requirement 'serve 8 concurrent users at 40 tokens/s each'. Batching is what breaks the memory wall: one decode step reads every weight once and serves the whole batch, so fixed weight traffic is amortised while compute, KV traffic, and all-reduce payload scale with the batch. It buys aggregate throughput, not per-sequence latency.
